answers.goal: My goal is to become an award-winning creative director, director, and photographer who specializes in fashion and beauty editorial and branded projects. I also hope to establish my own successful creative studio and agency, similar to Chandelier Creative in New York or SixTwentySix, the company I'm interning at now.
answers.drew:
I've always had a passion for the arts and creativity, and grew up making "movies" with my cousins and dance routines to show my parents. I've learned that I genuinely enjoy building projects and creating with other people. 

It's such a rewarding feeling to finish that opening show, or post that photo shoot online, knowing all the behind-the-scenes work that went into it, and the team you got to do it with. 

I also love the innate connection between the arts and culture, especially fashion, beauty, and music. I like to study music subgenres, music videos, fashion anthropology, and more, and understand the positive impact I can have by exploring these subjects through visual art. 

I can't imagine pursuing a career that doesn't revolve around creativity and expression.
answers.seeking:
Anyone who is genuinely passionate about their craft and who wants to build a creative community in LA. On Howard's campus, I've met so many creatives I know I can call on for collaboration, and I want to build a similar network here.

More specifically, early-to-mid-career professionals who are where I am now or where I hope to be in 5-10 years.
answers.inspiration:
I have so many, including Nina Simone, Lorna Simpson, Audre Lorde, Teyana Taylor, and Quinta Brunson. But my biggest is Bktherula, hands down. 

More than just her music being insane, I love her messaging. Listening to her music makes me feel confident in where I am, and in where I know I'm going. She emphasizes the importance of moving at your own pace, letting go of ego, knowing the value of your work, and following your passion. She's unapologetically herself, and her "LVL5" ideology is about living beyond your ego and having genuine compassion for others.

She pumps all of these messages into music that challenges traditional notions of femininity and mixes multiple subgenres, including melodic trap, pluggnb, and cloud rap. 

To me, BK helps me remember not to put myself in a box or limit my creativity out of fear that others won't understand it.
